answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A ferrous delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A tide check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A orchard penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 3774 identities need 3774 bonds of 65 tokens, 27119 dollars of hardware and 19 days of cover. It resembles a roll call where you must answer with the current news, so a recording played on loop gets caught
